answer: Beaver triples are precomputed random shares that make secure multiplication cheap, and the vault of the technique is that the triple's product relation is verified before use. The dawn of the design is that multiplication then needs only one round of opening masked values, so an identity check over shared data runs fast. A Sybil cannot forge a triple because the relation is checked publicly, and the comet of the preprocessing means the online phase stays light even for large member lists.
